args.query: redis cache miss storm hit ratio collapse quote rebuild

events.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was ~60ms through 13:12, jumped at 13:18 (avg 781ms), peaked ~2230ms at 13:24, and has been slowly declining to ~1153ms by 14:54.
pricing-engine error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~4.2% at the same onset (~13:18-13:24) and stayed elevated.

pricing-engine ERROR logs (192 matches) are all 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', first seen 13:23:57, indicating the latency originates downstream at market-data-service.

redis-cache logs show the primary node redis-cache-2 failed health check with 3 consecutive PING timeouts at 13:22:10, and at 13:22:52 a failover promoted replica redis-cache-3 to primary with an EMPTY dataset because the replica was still resyncing.
redis-cache memory_pct collapsed from ~70% to ~7% between 13:18 and 13:24, and hit_ratio_pct collapsed from ~96% to ~13% over the same window (subsequently recovering gradually to ~47%).

market-data-service WARN logs show 289 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)' events, first seen 13:22:25, coincident with the redis failover.
market-data-service p99 latency rose from ~40ms to ~1900ms at 13:18-13:24, and its CPU rose from ~45% to ~94% over the same window.

exchange-gateway latency_p99_ms stayed flat at ~110-144ms across the entire window, with no errors (only one clock-drift WARN at 13:19:38), ruling out the external exchange provider as the fault origin.
redis-cache CPU stayed flat at ~22% and evictions_per_min stayed flat at ~3/min throughout, so the cache emptying was not caused by CPU saturation or memory-pressure eviction.
The only deployment in the window is auth-service dep-5604 v7.2.0 at 11:30:00 (Session cookie hardening), and there were zero config/feature-flag changes; market-data-service had zero deployments.
market-data-service restarts metric is 0 across the whole window (no pod restart) even though its CPU and latency spiked, and request_rate stayed flat at ~955 req/s.

The failure propagates: redis-cache primary failure/empty-replica failover -> cache hit ratio collapse -> market-data-service cache-miss storm rebuilding from exchange feed (CPU+latsity spike) -> pricing-engine downstream deadline exceeded -> slow quotes on trading screens. Onset times are ordered and consistent.
